design.name: hoepa-prepayment-penalty-trigger epsilon boundary fixture (modeled on the art-234 L106 inverted-boundary class; constructed vectors, not a run against the live kernel)
design.pdk: 12-CFR-1026.32(a)(1)(iii) (HOEPA prepayment-penalty coverage trigger: penalty 'can exceed 2 percent')

metrics.operative_text: strict exceed: trigger only when the penalty CAN EXCEED 2 percent
metrics.boundary_case_frequency: exactly-2% caps are a common contractual term, so the boundary input is not exotic

observation.target: must not fire (2.0 does not exceed 2.0)

hypothesis: The float-safety epsilon was applied with the wrong sign for a strict comparator: '> t - eps' widens the trigger to include the boundary, converting strict > into >= at exactly t. An epsilon is part of the comparator, not a neutral safety margin — its sign decides which side of the boundary the test lands on.

candidates_considered.intervention: Keep 'pp_pct > 2.0 - 1e-5' on the ground that firing early is the conservative direction (flags more loans as high-cost).
candidates_considered.rejected_because: Concrete wrong verdict, not conservatism: on the fixture row pp_pct = 2.000 the code fires (2.000 > 1.99999) while the operative text is strict ('can exceed 2 percent'), so every loan whose penalty cap is exactly 2% — a common contractual cap — is misclassified as HOEPA-covered. A misclassification in either direction is a wrong verdict; conservative-direction is not compliance.

Fixes the stated boundary but reopens the float hazard the epsilon existed for: an input meant to be 2.0 that arrives as 2.0000000001 after upstream decimal arithmetic fires the trigger on noise. Cost visible in the fixture table: the no-epsilon form and the chosen form disagree on the 2.0-to-2.005 noise band, and only the chosen form states which side of that band is intended.

candidates_considered.intervention: Invert the epsilon to the strict side: 'pp_pct > 2.0 + 0.005', mirroring the same kernel family's points-and-fees trigger form ('> pf_limit + 0.005'), so the trigger fires only clearly above the threshold and the margin's direction is explicit.

metrics.vector_pp_2_000: old: FIRES (wrong, strict text) | chosen: no-fire (correct)
metrics.vector_pp_2_004: old: fires | chosen: no-fire (inside declared +0.005 noise margin)
metrics.vector_pp_2_005: old: fires | chosen: no-fire (boundary of the declared margin: 2.005 > 2.005 is false)
metrics.vector_pp_2_006: old: fires | chosen: FIRES (agree, clearly above threshold)
metrics.recompute_note: every cell recomputable from the two comparator strings and the input alone; e.g. row 2.000: old 2.000 > 1.99999 = true; chosen 2.000 > 2.005 = false

rationale: The at-boundary table is the whole argument: the two epsilon signs produce opposite verdicts at exactly 2.0, and only the strict-side form matches the operative text while still carrying an explicit, named noise margin. The fixture is synthetic by construction — the comparator shape and the strict-vs-epsilon analysis mirror a real audited kernel defect of this class, but the vectors here are constructed for calibration and were not executed against any live kernel; nothing in this episode claims a production measurement.
